correctness.rationale: A proper r-colouring of a complete r-partite graph must assign one distinct colour to each part. If at most r-2 parts are initially represented, no uncoloured vertex can see r-1 distinct neighbour colours, so no first force exists. If exactly r-1 parts are represented compatibly, every vertex in the missing part is forced to the unique unused colour, after which every remaining uncoloured vertex is forced; the all-r-parts case is immediate. For a fixed proper colouring, each seeded part contributes a nonempty subset and an unseeded part contributes the all-uncoloured state, giving the displayed product formulas without overcount because any forcing domain determines the unique missing colour. Fresh independent direct forcing enumeration on four representative multipartite types exactly matched the structural coefficient formulas.

final_claim: For every nonempty complete r-partite graph with r at least three and exactly r available colours, a partial assignment forces a total colouring exactly when it is compatible with a proper r-colouring and meets at least r-1 parts; this yields the stated closed domain-size generating polynomial, probability polynomial, minimum forcing-domain size r-1 and total count.
limitations: The theorem fixes the palette size to the number of nonempty parts and does not treat extra colours.
